fig_equity_time.webp.caption: Share of each year's single-country studies about low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): 17% in 2010 → 35% in 2025, against the 83% of global disease burden (GBD 2023 all-cause DALYs) those countries carry (dashed line). Full economic evaluations naming a single country with a known income group (26,126); 2026 is partial and left out. Income group: the World Bank classification in force on 1 January of the publication year (World Bank historical classifications).

fig_metric.webp.caption: Share of eligible evaluations reporting each comparable metric. The metric flips with income: high-income research reports QALYs (54%) and almost no DALYs (1%); low-income research does the reverse (39% DALYs, 7% QALYs) — so rich and poor settings are measured in different units. Base: 41,657 eligible evaluations (income shown for single-country studies, by the World Bank group in force on 1 January of the publication year); a study may report neither, one, or both.

fig_intervention_mix.webp.caption: Share of each income group's eligible single-country studies whose primary intervention class is the given type (the optional secondary class is not folded in). Pharmaceuticals peak in upper-middle-income settings (46.6%) and fall to 17.9% at low income, where they stay narrowly ahead of care-model and organisational evaluations (17.6%); vaccines rise steadily with lower income (4.7% → 14.0%) while surgery (13.8% → 7.8%) and devices (8.5% → 2.8%) fall. Base: 27,923 eligible single-country studies with a World Bank income group in force on 1 January of the publication year. Intervention classes were assigned by a large language model from each abstract (one pass), checked against a keyword list, the topic clusters and a second model; they have not been checked by people.

paper05.webp.caption: Percentage of each income group's disease-coded full economic evaluations that name each disease area, across the 14 harmonised groups (maternal & neonatal includes the MeSH pregnancy-complications branch C12.050.703; mental & substance use is MeSH F03). Rows run from areas most concentrated in low-income research (top) to high-income research (bottom): infectious disease dominates lower-income groups (79% of low-income and 61% of lower-middle-income studies), neoplasms and cardiovascular disease the high-income group. A study naming several areas appears in each, so columns sum above 100%. Income group: the World Bank classification in force on 1 January of the publication year.

fig_theme_rank.webp.caption: The 15 most-LMIC and 15 most-high-income of 73 research topics (found by clustering title-and-abstract embeddings) (all themes: 28%  LMIC). The high-income panel is shown first, plotted as each theme's high-income share (dementia leads at 93%); the LMIC panel as its LMIC share (malaria and dengue leads at 86%): 36%–86% LMIC vs 7%–16% LMIC. n per theme = single-country studies with a World Bank income group in force on 1 January of the publication year.
